This composite page covers **Region Midtjylland** (the administrative healthcare organization) and **Midtjylland** (the geographical and administrative region designation used in statistical tables). While they represent the same real-world area in Denmark, they are tracked as distinct entities within the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]] reporting framework. Region Midtjylland operates as the organizational body managing psychiatric services, including providers like [[dps-midtjylland|DPS Midtjylland]] [^src1], while "Midtjylland" serves as the regional label for aggregating performance data across local facilities such as [[bua-psykiatrisk-klinik-for-skoleboern|BUA Psykiatrisk Klinik for Skolebørn]] and [[bua-smaborn-klinik|BUA Psykiatrisk Klinik for Småbørn]] (also referenced as [[bua-smaborn-klinik|bua-smaborn]]) [^src2].

### The 2023 Data Crisis and Baseline Performance
In the 2023 reporting period, Region Midtjylland became a focal point of concern. It was the only region highlighted for a severe and notable drop in registered ADHD assessment processes, falling from 1,356 to 701 [^src1]. This drastic reduction was identified as a critical challenge for the validity of the database [^src1]. Under the regional designation of Midtjylland, the area recorded an extremely low fulfillment of [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] at just 36% [^src16]. Performance on other metrics was similarly mixed or poor: [[indikator-2b|Indikator 2b]] stood at 31% [^src3], and [[indikator-4|Indikator 4]] was fulfilled by only 7% of cases [^src4]. However, the region did achieve a 90% fulfillment rate for Indicator 2a [^src2] and reached [[50-percent|50-percent]] for [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] [^src4]. The reports also noted significant regional variations in the use of the [[agx01b|AGX01B]] process marker [^src6].

### The 2024 Turnaround and Practice Changes
By the 2024 report, Region Midtjylland demonstrated a significant turnaround, driven by deliberate administrative interventions. The organization implemented practice changes based on recommendations from the [[danske-multidisciplinaere-psykiatrigrupper-dmpger|Danske Multidisciplinære Psykiatrigrupper (DMPGer)]], specifically prioritizing somatic examinations [^src8]. Furthermore, the upward trends in the data were explicitly attributed to a focused effort on improving registration practices and an initiative to shorten the duration of ongoing assessment processes [^src7]. 

These operational shifts yielded substantial statistical improvements. Fulfillment of [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] in Midtjylland surged from 36% to 71% [^src8]. Similarly, [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] saw a massive increase of 32 percentage points, reaching 51% [^src10]. The region continued to report 50% for [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] [^src11] and achieved 50% for [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] [^src12], while [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]] reached an 80% fulfillment rate [^src14]. 

### Ongoing Challenges and Regional Variations
Despite these improvements, Midtjylland continues to face systemic challenges shared across Denmark. For instance, [[indikator-4|Indikator 4]] remained low at 6% [^src17], and no regions in the country, including Midtjylland, managed to fulfill the requirements for [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]] [^src13] or the adult population indicators for psychoeducation and psychotherapy [^src7]. Data anomalies also persist; there are vast regional differences in the use of the [[agx01b|AGX01B]] marker, with Region Midtjylland alone accounting for 142 rejected assessment processes between April 2024 and March 2025 [^src18]. When consulted for feedback on the latest annual report, Region Midtjylland responded that it had no comments [^src15].
